page.title: Samba / SMB destination
page.subtitle: Backup snapshots stream to an SMB/CIFS share on the configured server. Supports anonymous guest, basic user/password, and NTLMv2 domain authentication.
page.registerHint: This plugin owns one LocationType: samba. Pick an authentication method — guest for public shares, basic for workgroup auth, domain for Active Directory.

help.server: Hostname or IP of the Samba server (e.g. `nas.local` or `192.168.1.10`).
help.share: The share name as exported in smb.conf. The same name you would use with `smbclient //server/<share>`.
help.path: Subdirectory inside the share. Defaults to the share root (`/`). Snapshots are written directly under this path.
help.authMethod: How the plugin authenticates to the share. Guest uses a configured guest user; basic is NTLMv2 user/password against the workgroup; domain is NTLMv2 with an explicit Windows domain.
help.username: Samba or AD account. For domain auth, the bare username (no `DOMAIN\` prefix — use the Domain field).
help.password: Account password. Stored encrypted in the destination's cfg map.
help.domain: Windows / Active Directory domain. Used as the auth realm for NTLMv2.
help.guestUser: Account name sent on the wire for guest access. Defaults to `nobody` — match your Samba `guest account =` directive.
help.guestPassword: Password for the guest account. Usually empty; some configurations require a literal password.

setup.title: Samba / SMB setup guide
setup.subtitle: Steps below are tailored to the chosen authentication method. Switch the auth_method field to see alternative tracks.

step1.title: Verify TCP 445 is reachable
step1.body: From the host running McHarbor, run `Test-NetConnection nas.local -Port 445` (PowerShell) or `nc -zv nas.local 445` (bash). SMB/CIFS uses TCP 445; NetBIOS port 139 is legacy and rarely used by modern Samba.

step2.title: Pick or create a share
step2.body: If you already have a share named e.g. `backups`, note its name. To create one, add to /etc/samba/smb.conf on the server: `[backups] path = /srv/backups browseable = yes read only = no` then `sudo systemctl restart smbd`.

step3.title: Save the destination
step3.body: In McHarbor, fill in Server (hostname or IP), Share, and Path (defaults to the share root). Pick the authentication method that matches your share policy, then save.

step1.title: Enable guest access on the share
step1.body: In smb.conf, add `guest ok = yes` to the share block and set `map to guest = bad user` globally. By default Samba uses `nobody` as the guest user; override with `guest account = ...` if you have a custom account.

step2.title: Test from another host
step2.body: Try `smbclient //nas.local/backups -U nobody%""` from a Linux box to confirm guest access works. The McHarbor plugin will send the same credentials.

step1.title: Create a local Samba user
step1.body: Run `sudo smbpasswd -a backup-user` on the server. The password you set is what the operator types into McHarbor — both Samba and the system account store the same hash.

step2.title: Grant the user write access to the share path
step2.body: Set filesystem ownership: `sudo chown -R backup-user:backup-user /srv/backups`. The McHarbor plugin runs as the configured user, so read+write at the OS layer is required even if smb.conf allows the user.

step1.title: Join the Samba server to the AD domain
step1.body: Use `net ads join -U administrator` (or `samba-tool domain join`) on the Samba host. Confirm `wbinfo -u` lists domain users. The McHarbor plugin needs the Samba server to validate NTLMv2 against AD, not against the local SAM.

step2.title: Grant the backup user access to the share
step2.body: In smb.conf, set `valid users = @CORP\backup-users` (or specific UPNs) on the share block. The McHarbor plugin will send the username in the form you configure here — `DOMAIN\user` is NOT supported; use the bare username + the Domain field.

setup.footer: go-smb2 v1.x does not negotiate SMB3 encryption. Use a private LAN/VPN for the share, or front it with a TLS tunnel (stunnel, wireguard) if cross-internet writes are required.

error.noUsername: Username is required for this authentication method.
error.noPassword: Password is required for this authentication method.
error.noDomain: Domain is required for domain authentication.
error.mountFailed: Could not mount the share. Verify server, share name, and credentials.
error.permissionDenied: SMB server rejected the operation. Check the user's write permission on the share.
